content: Linezolid is an antibiotic that works by inhibiting the growth of certain bacteria by preventing them from producing proteins essential for their survival. It is commonly used to treat infections such as pneumonia, skin infections, and infections caused by bacteria resistant to other antibiotics. However, its use may not be appropriate for all infections, as some bacteria may have developed resistance to linezolid. Linezolid is available in various forms, including 600 mg oral tablets, 100 mg/5 mL oral suspension, and injectable formulations. It should be stored at room temperature (68°F to 77°F or 20°C to 25°C) in a cool, dry place, protected from light. The oral liquid should not be shaken but gently inverted 3 to 5 times before measuring the dose with an accurate measuring device. Common side effects of linezolid include nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, headache, and anemia. Serious side effects, though less common, include severe allergic reactions, myelosuppression (reduced blood cell production), serotonin syndrome, peripheral and optic neuropathy, seizures, antibiotic-associated diarrhea, low sodium levels (hyponatremia), and lactic acidosis. Patients should immediately report symptoms such as breathing difficulties, swelling, vision changes, muscle twitching, confusion, or severe diarrhea to their healthcare provider. Linezolid interacts with certain medications and foods. It increases serotonin levels in the body, which can lead to serotonin syndrome when combined with serotonergic drugs such as SSRIs, SNRIs, or MAO inhibitors. It should not be taken with large amounts of tyramine-rich foods (e.g., aged cheeses, red wine, smoked meats) to avoid hypertensive episodes. Patients should inform their healthcare provider about all medications, supplements, and health conditions before starting linezolid. Linezolid is not recommended for use in patients with uncontrolled hypertension, pheochromocytoma, or certain other conditions. It should be used cautiously in patients with diabetes, thyroid problems, seizure disorders, or carcinoid syndrome. Pregnant and breastfeeding women should consult their healthcare provider before using linezolid, as it passes into breast milk and may affect the infant. In case of overdose, seek immediate medical attention. Linezolid should only be used as prescribed and not shared with others.
